messages:
Alex: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of pods stuck Pending in eu-west GPU pool. Root msg: 0/6 nodes fit: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu and also 0/6 Insufficient memory in several events.
Maria: Can you paste the `kubectl describe` events for one of the pending pods?
Alex: Sure, snippet below:
```
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal  NotTriggerScaleUp  2m    cluster-autoscaler  pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims
  Normal  FailedScheduling  2m     default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 4 Insufficient memory.
```
Maria: autoscaler log?
k8s-autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale up request registered for nodepool-gpu-burst, desired=+2 (reason: insufficient resources for pending pods)
Ben: This looks like the classic burst->oversize->fragmentation loop. Short-lived jobs request 1 GPU but request high memory/cpu too, then CA spins up nodes that end up ~30% utilized and never get packed before scale-down.
Julie: Do we have scale-down-delay and balance-similar-node-pools enabled? I remember nodepool-gpu-burst has aggressive scale-down (300s) but AZ spread means new nodes land in different racks so packing suffers.
Alex: Config: `scale-down-delay=5m`, `max-nodes=12`, `min-nodes=2` for that pool. Also a lot of pods come with CPU/memory requests much higher than their steady state — telemetry from infra-observability shows median memory request is 14GB but actual RSS is ~6GB for those jobs.
infra-observability: last24h metrics: binpacking_efficiency_p95=62%, avg_node_gpu_util=0.36, pending_peak=18 pods. Cost impact estimated ~+18% on spot spend due to fragmented nodes.
Maria: Two quick mitigations: 1) introduce a tiny warm pool (prewarmed nodes) to absorb spikes, 2) enforce stricter requests==limits for GPU jobs so scheduler can pack them deterministically.
Ben: Also consider a separate nodepool with `burst=true` taint and a low-priority toleration so non-latency-critical batch jobs land there. That reduces cross-pool packing churn.
Julie: Would enabling binpack by label help? e.g., `k8s.alpha.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled` on warm nodes + `topologySpreadConstraints` so pods co-locate on fewer nodes? Might be hacky.
Alex: Also noticed many jobs set requests: `cpu: 16` `memory: 32Gi` but only need ~4cpu/8Gi in practice. We should run a quota enforcement job that warns devs and suggests right-sizing.
Maria: Long term: predictive warm pool — use short-term forecast from recent submit rates to keep 1-2 spare nodes ready in each region. For now, I can flip CA config to increase consolidation window to 8m so it waits a bit before scaling down.
Ben: Watch out — increasing consolidation window will raise cost if burst patterns are infrequent. Maybe combine with a 2-node preemptible pool (cheaper) and a lower eviction priority so it's the one to be scaled down first.
k8s-autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler: applied change to nodepool-gpu-burst: scale-down-delay increased to 8m (manual-by: Maria)
Alex: After change I see one new node created and some pending pods scheduled — good sign. We'll monitor 1h.
Julie: ACTIONS: (1) Maria to create runbook for warm pool + autoscaler knob (2) Ben to prototype burst-tainted nodepool and toleration strategy (3) Alex to open a PR with a telemetry dashboard that surfaces request vs actual for GPU workloads.
Alex: Also sending a short note to ML teams: please set requests closer to actual usage or use burst nodepool label for ephemeral experiments.
Maria: +1. I'll also add a Lighthouse alert if pending pods > 10 for 10m. :rotating_light:
Ben: If this reoccurs we should consider a scheduler extender that packs by predicted memory usage instead of requested memory (risky), or an admission controller to auto-rightsize ephemeral runs.
Julie: Ok closing for now, will re-evaluate after 1h and post follow-up. :thumbsup:
